title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk

epigraph.quote: In insurance and healthcare services, revenue is a vanity metric; medical care ratio, reserve development, and contract backlog tell you whether the engine is healthy or burning oil.
epigraph.author: Healthcare Forensic Checklist

web_blocks.html: UnitedHealth Group's consolidated GAAP earnings can be masked by one-time items. Recent examples include divestiture losses ($8.3B in FY2024), cyberattack charges ($2.9B in FY2024), and $2.5B in total FY2025 restructuring and reserve charges (which includes the $1.4B SG&A restructuring component cited in Chapter 3) [1, 2, 7]. Because of those distortions, institutional analysts track six leading operational KPIs to measure underlying momentum [1, 2, 7].

web_blocks.caption: UNH Core Operational KPI Dashboard (FY2023–Q3 2026)
rows: Stabilizing: down 150 bps YoY vs Q3 2025 (89.9%), aided by $610M favorable reserve development [7]
Improving: down 70 bps YoY from 13.5% in Q3 2025 via administrative & AI automation [7]
Intentional pruning: -1.46M YTD 2026 (-935K MA, -685K Medicaid) to exit loss-making markets [7]
Watchpoint: above industry average (~68% in 4+ Stars), preserving 2028 quality bonus payments [7, 19]

web_blocks.takeaway: The 2025 MCR spike to 88.9% was the main driver of the earnings reset. Through Q3 2026, MCR turned downward to 88.4% versus 89.9% a year earlier. Meanwhile, Days Claims Payable held steady at 47.0 days, and Optum Insight's margin expansion offset Rx volume attrition.

web_blocks.html: For over two decades, UNH's hallmark was 'beat-and-raise' guidance reliability, targeting 13%–16% long-term adjusted EPS growth. That credibility shattered in 2024–2025 [7, 14]. Returning CEO Stephen J. Hemsley and CFO Wayne DeVeydt then began methodically rebuilding it in 2026 [7, 14].

web_blocks.takeaway: Management's 2025 guidance collapse was a severe credibility shock. In response, Hemsley's 2026 reset set a conservative floor (>$17.75) and beat it by $2.75+ per share within nine months.

web_blocks.title: Structural Potential Beyond the 2026 Reset
paragraphs: Three structural catalysts support multi-year normalization after 2026. First, CMS finalized a +2.48% net average Medicare Advantage rate increase for CY2027, adding over $13 billion in industry funding versus a near-flat +0.09% proposal [18]. Second, UNH's 2027 Star Ratings kept >=69% of members in 4+ Star plans, protecting 2028 quality bonus revenue [7]. Third, Optum Insight's AI-enabled coding and digital prior-authorization tools are lifting operating margins above 22% [7, 9].

book_paragraphs: If you and I want to know whether UnitedHealth Group's 2026 recovery is real or an accounting mirage, we cannot rely on headline earnings per share alone. In a conglomerate of this size, GAAP earnings can swing wildly on one-off items. One year brings an $8 billion Latin American divestiture write-off, while the next brings $400 million foundation gifts or reserve releases. Instead, we must pop the hood and inspect six operational gauges that cannot be easily faked.

The single most important gauge is the Medical Care Ratio—the share of every premium dollar spent directly on medical care. For years, UNH ran like clockwork in the 82% to 84% range. In 2024 it crept up to 85.5%. In 2025 it jumped to 88.9% as Medicare Advantage utilization surged and CMS's V28 coding cuts bit into revenue. In Q3 2026, that ratio finally bent back in the right direction. It dropped 150 basis points year-over-year to 88.4%, aided by $610 million in favorable prior-period reserve development. Meanwhile, Days Claims Payable—a check on whether an insurer is under-reserving for unpaid bills—held steady at 47.0 days.

The second gauge is membership discipline. Between December 2025 and September 2026, UnitedHealthcare's medical membership shrank from 49.8 million to 48.3 million. That drop included a 935,000-member contraction in Medicare Advantage and a 685,000-member drop in Medicaid. Normally, losing 1.5 million customers would alarm you and me. Here, it is proof of discipline. Hemsley's team deliberately exited unprofitable counties and repriced money-losing contracts rather than chasing empty top-line volume.

Now let's audit management's credibility—what you and I call the walk-the-talk test. For fifteen years, UNH's leadership team was treated as infallible because they consistently beat and raised annual guidance. Then came 2025. Management entered the year guiding for $29.50 to $30.00 in adjusted EPS, cut it in April, and suspended guidance altogether in May when Andrew Witty resigned. They ultimately delivered $16.35. That was a historic forecasting failure. Yet look at how Stephen Hemsley and CFO Wayne DeVeydt handled 2026. They set a conservative floor of $17.75 in January 2026, raised it to $19.50–$20.00 in July, and raised it again to at least $20.50 in October after delivering $18.30 in nine months.

Looking ahead, the structural runway is clearing, though not without watchpoints. CMS's April 2026 final rate notice for 2027 delivered a +2.48% payment increase, far better than the flat +0.09% initial proposal. UNH also kept at least 69% of its Medicare Advantage members in 4-star or higher plans for 2027. Combined with Optum Insight's 22.6% operating margins, the operational dials are turning back toward health. The main caveat is that DOJ Medicare billing probes must not impose material structural limits.

Let's also watch two subtler operational KPIs that separate a durable turnaround from a brief bounce: Optum Insight's contract backlog and Optum Rx's script mix. Optum Insight's backlog held above $32 billion even through the Change Healthcare cyberattack. Its July 2026 purchase of Alegeus also deepens its consumer-directed HSA and FSA footprint alongside Optum Bank. Meanwhile, Optum Rx's quarterly adjusted scripts dipped 5% year-over-year to 393 million in Q3 2026 purely because UnitedHealthcare shed unprofitable lives. Even so, Optum Rx's operating earnings rose 11% year-over-year to $1.72 billion on biosimilar adoption and specialty execution. When a segment grows profit by double digits despite a 5% volume headwind, the underlying engine is working. Tracking those six operational gauges quarter by quarter gives you an objective scoreboard before headline GAAP earnings catch up.

book_callouts.title: Under-Promise, Over-Deliver Returns
book_callouts.text: After the credibility shock of suspending 2025 guidance in May 2025, Hemsley's 2026 guidance cadence restored a classic conservative buffer—raising full-year adjusted EPS expectations from >$17.75 in January to >=$20.50 by October.
bullets: Q3 2026 MCR: 88.4% (down 150 bps YoY) with 47.0 Days Claims Payable.
Q3 2026 Operating Cost Ratio: 12.8% (down 70 bps YoY).
CY2027 CMS MA Final Rate: +2.48% net increase (vs +0.09% Advance Notice).
